server-modes-12.title: How should beginners choose a server?
server-modes-12.text: Choose PvE to learn gathering and building: players cannot attack one another, and bases with a Tool Cupboard cannot be raided or destroyed by other players. Choose PvP for combat and raiding. Before joining, check resource rates, wipe frequency and the No PC tag, which means PC players are not allowed on that server.

newbie-servers-105.title: Why has my newbie server disappeared?
newbie-servers-105.text: Newbie servers are temporary learning environments. When their opening period ends, they are permanently removed from the list along with the wipe and cannot be restored. Use them to learn the basics rather than as a server for long-term progress.

server-wipe-8.title: What is a wipe, and where can I check its time?
server-wipe-8.text: A wipe regularly resets server data, clearing buildings, loot and debris from the map for a new survival cycle. In the lobby, open the server list and select the server you want to join. Its details show the creation time and the scheduled time of the next wipe.

solo-duo-trio-248.title: What limits apply on Solo, Duo and Trio servers?
solo-duo-trio-248.text: SOLO, DUO and TRIO limit groups to one, two and three players respectively. The limits also apply to Tool Cupboard authorization and code-lock users. Once full, a lock may refuse a friend even with the correct code. Changing the code or picking up and replacing the door clears the user list; players must then enter the code again. Teaming beyond the limit breaks these servers' rules.

base-upkeep-245.title: Why is my base upkeep getting more expensive?
base-upkeep-245.text: On PvP servers, more structural pieces increase the upkeep surcharge; the largest size bracket can cost twice the base amount. Authorizing more than four players in the cupboard adds a further surcharge. Doors and hatches need upkeep but do not count toward the size bracket. PvE has no such surcharges. Check the cupboard's daily cost for the resources currently required.

building-privileges-191.title: Why can't I build despite having cupboard authorization?
building-privileges-191.text: A cupboard's build zone follows foundations, walls and floors rather than forming a fixed circle around the cupboard. Where several protected zones overlap, the building containing the oldest structural piece determines building permission. Authorization in another nearby cupboard may therefore be insufficient. Walk around and watch the building status indicator to find the boundary.

merge-buildings-190.title: How can separated buildings be merged again?
merge-buildings-190.text: Restoring full side-to-side contact between structural pieces lets the system treat them as one building again. This usually works for a base that was originally connected and later damaged; separately started buildings are difficult to align precisely. After merging, one cupboard and one build zone remain, and the extra cupboard in the absorbed section is removed.

rebuild-debris-200.title: Why can't I immediately replace a destroyed wall?
rebuild-debris-200.text: Destroyed building pieces briefly leave debris that blocks new construction in the same spot. Wait for the construction-blocked countdown to end; the official guide gives about 30 seconds. For some walls, the debris may clear sooner if the supporting pieces are also destroyed.

fence-snapping-209.title: How can I reduce gaps between fences?
fence-snapping-209.text: When placing fences, adjacent sections now snap together and align automatically. This makes a continuous perimeter easier to build and reduces gaps enemies can peek or shoot through. The source describes alignment during placement; it does not say that existing gaps repair themselves.

signal-airdrop-249.title: How do I call an airdrop with a signal flare gun?
signal-airdrop-249.text: The signal flare gun is found only in loot and cannot be crafted. Fire toward open sky at least 45 degrees above the horizon, avoiding roofs, bridges and rock faces. After a successful shot, the plane arrives in roughly one to two minutes and the drop lands near the firing position. Other players may notice the signal, so choose somewhere you can defend while waiting.

first-day-progression.title: Your first day: make tools, then build a small home
first-day-progression.text: Start with wood, stone and food, make basic gathering tools, then choose a resource-accessible spot with fewer passing players for a small home. Gather materials before building so you do not run out halfway. Once you have storage, take only essentials outside and return to deposit a good haul. Invest in expensive gear and major expansion after gathering and storage are reliable.

gather-hit-markers-116.title: Follow the markers when chopping trees and mining
gather-hit-markers-116.text: With ordinary tools, hit a tree once, then aim the next strike at the red trunk marker for more resources and faster felling. Stone and ore nodes show a glowing spot that moves after a successful hit. Locate it again after each hit instead of holding attack on the same spot.

workbench-research-path-243.title: Select your target technology to see the full research cost
workbench-research-path-243.text: Select the equipment you want in the technology tree, even if prerequisites remain locked. The screen shows the remaining scrap cost of the entire path. Confirming researches the missing prerequisites and the target together. Check the total before spending. Actual research requires a workbench within about five metres; opening the tree farther away is view-only and spends nothing.

solo-base-core-upgrades.title: Solo building: strengthen the core before the outer layers
solo-base-core-upgrades.text: With limited solo resources, put the Tool Cupboard deep inside the core. Upgrade the core structures to stone first, then gradually to metal, while strengthening the doors. Add outer defensive layers once the core is secure. Tuck furnaces into corners to leave walking room. The author's design uses an entrance buffer room to reduce direct exposure of the interior when checking outside.

spread-base-loot-83.title: Spread valuables around your base to limit losses from one breach
spread-base-loot-83.text: Add defensive layers outside important rooms so attackers must break through more obstacles. Store valuables in different parts of the base instead of risking everything at a single breach. The Tool Cupboard remains a priority: keep it protected and locked. Spreading loot reduces the damage from one breach; it does not guarantee that supplies survive a complete raid.

turret-placement-247.title: Aim turrets at doors and corridors, then check ammunition
turret-placement-247.text: While placing a turret, use the translucent sector on the ground to aim it at a doorway or a corridor enemies must cross. Load the correct ammunition and check the remaining rounds when restocking the cupboard: an empty turret will not fire. Teammates need authorization in the cupboard covering the turret or may become targets. Crafting also consumes the actual weapon in the recipe, so include it in your budget.

backup-supplies-84.title: Keep backup supplies elsewhere in case your base falls
backup-supplies-84.text: Besides defending your main base, keep basic supplies in another hidden location so a bad night does not force a complete restart. Travel with others when carrying valuable cargo. This preparation addresses what happens after the main base falls: supplies spread inside it can still all be lost, while a separate reserve offers another route to recovery.

raid-preparation.title: Check four equipment groups before a raid
raid-preparation.text: Before leaving, check your primary weapon and spare ammunition, backup weapon, breaching rockets or C4, and armor and supplies. Prepare medkits, bandages, water and sleeping bags, and repair worn gear first. Do not take all your most valuable items at once; keep emergency equipment in reserve. Consider retaliation when choosing targets: a base close to home is not necessarily a good choice.

player-shop-stock-79.title: Check player shops on the map before travelling
player-shop-stock-79.text: Open the map and select a player shop icon to check goods and prices before making the trip. The marker disappears when the shop sells out. When running your own shop, place the vending machine within a cupboard's zone or others may take goods and earnings from the back. Empty the earnings storage regularly; trades stop when it is full.

quarry-collection-80.title: Collect quarry output regularly after adding fuel
quarry-collection-80.text: After unlocking the Mining Quarry blueprint, gather the materials and craft it on the server; buying it in the main shop does not give you a finished machine. Place it and add fuel to produce stone and ores. Running it makes noise that attracts enemies, and other players may take resources left inside. Protect the surroundings and collect the output promptly.

car-start-246.title: Starting a roadside car: find a motor and fit a battery
car-start-246.html:
Find abandoned cars along roads and near locations. You need a battery, a motor and Fuel Bottles. Research and craft the battery; motors cannot be crafted and must be found under roadside car hoods. Open the hood, install both parts and add fuel to the car's fuel slot.

Seat counts vary. Passengers can use weapons, but drivers cannot. The boot cannot be locked, so anyone can take its contents. Use it for temporary transport, remove valuables when parking, and remember that someone else can drive the car away.

vehicle-fuel-252.title: Car won't refuel? Check which fuel you have
vehicle-fuel-252.html:
Copters, buggies, roadside cars, trains and mining quarries use Fuel Bottles. Factory fuel is a different item and cannot go into vehicle fuel slots. Check the item before trying again.

Fuel Bottles need no research and can also be found in loot. Hunting provides Animal Fat for crafting; check the crafting menu for materials and batch output. Refuel and bring spare bottles before a long trip.

double-barrel-position-250.title: Double Barrel: fight up close and plan your reload
double-barrel-position-250.html:
The Double Barrel holds two shells and fires one barrel at a time. Use it at doorways and in corridors; effectiveness falls with distance, so avoid chasing distant enemies across open ground.

Choose cover you can retreat behind before engaging. After two shots you must reload: avoid doing so in the middle of a doorway. Research the weapon at a workbench before crafting it, and pack compatible shells.

recycler-output-full-81.title: Recycler stopped? Check the output slots
recycler-output-full-81.html:
Recyclers are found at gas stations, the Miner, the Forester and in towns. Insert recyclable items and start the machine; raw resources cannot be recycled. Each slot shows progress and remaining time.

When output slots are full, the machine stops without consuming more input or dropping output on the ground. Collect the materials and restart it. Recycling ammunition can lose some materials, so don't expect a full refund. The running machine makes noise: watch for nearby players.

quarry-decay-194.title: Quarry losing health? Check cupboard protection
quarry-decay-194.html:
A regular mining quarry decays outside Tool Cupboard protection or when the cupboard lacks upkeep resources. Fuel does not provide maintenance protection. Check both its location and the cupboard's supplies.

Place it on or directly beside a protected building and check the building status indicator there. Refill upkeep before logging out and check again after a long absence, so decay does not destroy the quarry before you collect its output.

pve-chest-access-206.title: PvE teammate can't open chests? Check cupboard authorization
pve-chest-access-206.html:
On PvE servers, chests inside a protected building can be opened only by the Tool Cupboard owner and authorized players. If a teammate can enter but cannot open chests, check their authorization.

This protection depends on cupboard coverage. Chests outside that area do not have the same protection; choosing PvE does not make storage safe everywhere.

clan-station-owner-211.title: Agree who places clan production stations
clan-station-owner-211.html:
Clan sawmills, scrap recyclers and quarries are unlocked in the clan progression tree and placed by the leader or an officer. Each clan can have one of each type per server. Agree who will manage it: only the placer can open, fuel, start and collect from it, even if another member is the leader.

Stations use Low Grade Fuel. Starting reserves clan currency for the loaded fuel; stopping refunds the unused portion. Stop before refueling because the fuel slot is locked while running. Use the panel button. Empty fuel, full storage or a server restart means you must start it again.

Keep a Tool Cupboard nearby and collect output regularly. Stations cannot be locked and enemies can destroy them, dropping the contents and fuel. Clan-level production improvements apply while stopped; check the station after an upgrade before restarting.

clan-vault-access-198.title: Clan warehouse: why can I deposit but not withdraw?
clan-vault-access-198.html:
Clan storage holds weapons, attachments, components and resources. Every member can deposit from their personal Safe, but withdrawals need permission from the leader. If you can only deposit, ask the leader to check the warehouse access list.

Storage is shared across servers. Some clan perks and opened Allowance rewards also supply it. Granting or revoking access notifies the clan, so agree who collects and distributes supplies.

clan-shop-216.title: Using the clan shop: where do rewards go?
clan-shop-216.html:
Open the shop from the clan menu and spend currency earned through clan activities and progression. Higher clan levels unlock more stock. Some purchases have weekly or total limits; check the remaining allowance first.

Rewards are for the clan. Resources go to the clan warehouse, not necessarily your backpack. Check the item description and warehouse, then have an authorized member withdraw them.

death-marker-recovery-120.title: Recovering loot: check the death marker first
death-marker-recovery-120.html:
After dying, check the map marker and coordinates. Compare them with the numbered sleeping bags to choose a useful respawn point instead of relying only on the direction you remember running.

The marker locates the spot but does not guarantee your loot remains. Bring essential supplies and check whether enemies are still nearby before approaching to recover items.

team-invite-26.title: Inviting teammates in person or remotely
team-invite-26.html:
Approach the player on the server until the interaction icon appears, then press the action button to send a team invitation. They must accept; standing nearby does not automatically form a team.

For a clanmate, open the player list, find their nickname and select Invite to Team from the three-dot menu. You need not meet in person. Clan membership and team membership are separate.

deathmatch-practice-162.title: Practice shooting in DeathMatch before heading out
deathmatch-practice-162.html:
Choose DeathMatch (DM) or Team DeathMatch (TDM) in the server list to practice aiming, firing and reloading. Armor, rifles, ammunition and medical supplies are provided; no gathering or base building is needed. Crafting, the shop and the Safe are disabled.

DM is free-for-all: the first player to 30 kills wins. In TDM, the first team to 100 kills wins and friendly fire is disabled. Kills restore health and ammunition; respawns have brief protection. Practice controls here, then return to survival servers to practice supply management and retreating.

firing-controls-98.title: Adjust firing controls for each weapon type
firing-controls-98.html:
In Controls & HUD, set crossbows, shotguns and rifles separately to Tap, Hold or Release. Adjust one familiar weapon and try it before changing the others.

The button editor lets you move and resize controls but is available only from the lobby. Sprint mode, Auto ADS and Auto Reload can be changed during a match. For inventory management, enable double-tap item movement and adjust its timing.

aim-sensitivity-99.title: Unsteady aim? Adjust sensitivity by sight type
aim-sensitivity-99.html:
The Sensitivity tab has separate settings for general view, iron and handmade sights, holosights and optical scopes. If only one sight feels wrong, change that setting without disturbing the others.

Choose gyroscope Off, While ADS or Always, with separate sight sensitivities. Acceleration, camera smoothing and axis inversion are also available. Make small changes and test your aim; recheck values if an update changes the feel.

graphics-fps-100.title: Low FPS? Start with draw distance and shadows
graphics-fps-100.html:
In the lobby, use Re-adjust Graphics to match settings to your device. For manual changes, lower draw distance first, then graphics quality and shadows. If needed, lower resolution or disable post-processing.

These graphics options can be changed through the pause menu without leaving the server. If lowering quality does not help, check your connection and background apps. Heat can reduce performance too. Distinguish choppy rendering from network delay before adjusting more settings.

base-notifications-101.title: Enable base attack and upkeep notifications before logging out
base-notifications-101.html:
In Notifications, enable the master switch, then attack, decay and wipe alerts. Attack alerts help you notice raids; decay alerts prompt you to check cupboard resources; wipe alerts help you plan supplies.

Friend activity, map events and in-game pop-ups have separate controls. If pop-ups distract you, adjust those instead of disabling everything. Alerts only help you notice trouble: check locks and upkeep before leaving.

building-rotation-59.title: Building piece won't line up? Hold Rotate
building-rotation-59.html:
In Build mode, select a piece before adjusting its orientation. Tapping Rotate turns it 45 degrees; holding rotates smoothly for finer placement. Check the preview before placing to avoid rebuilding.

The center of the screen shows the resource cost: green means sufficient materials, red means insufficient. Check orientation, cost and placement preview together rather than merely checking for wood in your inventory.

key-code-lock-choice-62.title: Which lock should you use alone or with teammates?
key-code-lock-choice-62.html:
A Key Lock allows only its owner to open it with the matching key and cannot serve as a shared entrance. It suits solo use; consider a Code Lock for teammates who need regular access.

Code Locks fit doors, cupboards and large storage boxes. Share the code only with trusted players. Protect the Tool Cupboard especially carefully because access also affects building privileges.

first-aid-preparation-71.title: Put bandages and medkits in quick slots before leaving
first-aid-preparation-71.html:
Bandages use cloth and require no workbench research, making them useful early supplies. Medkits restore more health but need their blueprint unlocked. Research and craft them before entering combat areas, not after you are injured.

Consume either item from the inventory or put it in a quick slot and use the action button. Check quantities and slot positions before leaving. Find exact material costs in the crafting menu or the site's calculator.

Research and craft them before entering combat areas, not after you are injured. Consume either item from the inventory or put it in a quick slot and use the action button. Check quantities and slot positions before leaving. Find exact material costs in the crafting menu or the site's calculator.

sound-direction-223.title: Can't locate footsteps? Enable sound visualization
sound-direction-223.html:
Sound visualization adds directional indicators for nearby gunshots, footsteps and other noises. Use them as clues when you hear movement but do not know where to look.

Go to Settings → Audio → Additional → Visualization of Sound Effects. You can change it during a match and star it for quick access from Favourites. The indicators show sound direction, not an enemy's precise position.

headset-microphone-102.title: Bluetooth headset connected, but teammates can't hear you?
headset-microphone-102.html:
Check Headset Mic in Audio settings. Enabling it captures speech through the connected headset microphone rather than the phone's built-in microphone. It is off by default.

If no voice gets through, return to the lobby and check Microphone Access in System settings. The System tab is unavailable during a match. Ask a teammate to confirm the sound before starting an activity that needs voice coordination.

offscreen-teammates-111.title: See teammate direction without repeatedly opening the map
offscreen-teammates-111.html:
Enable Off-Screen Marker under Settings → Basic → In Game Display. When teammates are outside your view, edge markers show which direction they are in as you move.

You can change this during a match. It is separate from the map's teammate visibility switch. Open the map when you need their actual map position.

default-skin-159.title: Set a default skin for crafting and pickups
default-skin-159.html:
In the lobby, tap the skin button to the right of your character. Select Weapons, Armor or Building Items, choose an item and an owned skin, then set it as default. You won't need to choose it again each time you craft that item.

The default also applies to skinless versions you pick up and to your starting hatchet and torch when joining a server. It changes appearance only; it does not give you equipment or unlock its blueprint.

sandbox-save-238.title: Practice building in the Sandbox, and save before leaving
sandbox-save-238.html:
Choose Sandbox in the server list or open it through Settings → System. Building and crafting cost no resources. Select structural materials directly and demolish pieces to adjust rooms and passages.

There are three save slots and no autosave. Save and load manually; declining to save on exit loses your changes. Saves stay on the device rather than syncing with your account, so consider this before reinstalling or switching phones.

This guide covers layouts and saves only. Official pages disagree about explosion damage testing, so we do not treat the Sandbox as a verified way to measure raid costs.

leave-clan-179.title: Changing clans? Plan your departure and leadership transfer
leave-clan-179.html:
Open the clan member list, tap the three dots beside your name and choose Leave Clan. You must wait two hours before joining another clan, so allow for that when planning with a new group.

If the leader wants the clan to continue, transfer leadership before leaving. Do not kick everyone simply to leave. The clan automatically disbands when its last member leaves.

free-drop-rewards-236.title: Claim unlocked lobby rewards before they expire
free-drop-rewards-236.html:
When FREE DROP appears in the lobby, check its progress and remaining time. Follow the event's viewing instructions to earn points. Claim each unlocked reward manually: unclaimed rewards disappear when the timer ends.

A skin you already own is replaced by silver. Daily point limits can temporarily disable the button, and points may arrive late; unlocked rewards remain claimable. An event starting during a match appears when you next return to the lobby.

replay-tutorial-103.title: Skipped the tutorial? Replay it from the lobby
replay-tutorial-103.html:
From the lobby, go to Settings → System, find Complete Tutorial and press GO. Use it if you skipped the introduction or need a refresher after time away.

It covers gathering, crafting tools and weapons, and building. The System tab is absent from the in-match pause menu, so return to the lobby to find it. You do not need another account.
